title: Lipid Bilayer Vesicle Generation Using Microfluidic Jetting
protocol: Design the infinity chamber using CAD software compatible with a laser cutter.
Separate two circles of diameter 0.183 in by a center-to-center distance of 0.15 in.
Cut the chamber from 1/8-3/16 in clear acrylic using a laser cutter.
Drill a 1/16 in hole through the edge of the acrylic chamber to the infinity-shaped well.
Repeat drilling on the opposite side.
Cut a small rectangle from a 0.2 mm acrylic sheet with scissors or a laser cutter.
Apply a thin but complete layer of quick-drying adhesive to one side of the 0.2 mm acrylic.
Glue the 0.2 mm acrylic to the bottom of the chamber, ensuring it covers the infinity chamber cutout and aligns flush with the edge of the chamber wall.
Cut two small pieces of natural rubber to cover the drilled holes.
Apply quick-drying adhesive around the hole.
Place the rubber over the hole and press on all areas with a pair of forceps to secure.
Repeat for both drilled holes.
Poke a hole in the natural rubber on both sides of the chamber using a 23 G, 1 in needle to facilitate insertion of the piezoelectric inkjet tip.
Store stock lipid solution in chloroform in a -20 °C freezer.
Transfer the lipid from a stock vial to a small glass jar and gently dry under argon or nitrogen.
Hold the jar at an angle while drying to expose more surface area to the gas, allowing the lipid to dry faster.
Allow the dried solution to sit under vacuum in a desiccator for 1-2 hr with the cap of the jar only slightly screwed on.
Add n-decane to resolubilize the lipid at 25 mg/ml.
Vortex the lipid solution briefly and sonicate it in a bath sonicator for 15 min.
Store the reconstituted lipid in n-decane at -20 °C.
Prepare a stock sucrose solution by adding 900 µl of 300 mM sucrose and 100 µl of 1% methylcellulose to a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Draw the sucrose solution into a disposable 1 ml plastic syringe.
Holding the syringe with the tip facing upwards, flick the shaft repeatedly to expel any bubbles toward the tip and push the plunger to eject trapped air.
Install a 0.22 µm filter on the end of the syringe.
Hold the syringe vertically and push the plunger until a droplet is formed above the tip to prevent air from being trapped in the filter.
Unscrew the female Luer adapter of the inkjet and securely press it in place over the end of the filter.
Eject fluid again to prevent trapping air inside the filter.
Screw in the top of the inkjet, ensuring that fluid travels to the tip after complete attachment.
Mount the syringe assembly on the microscope stage using a v-clamp.
Attach the wire from the inkjet to the inkjet controller.
Determine the magnification and necessary lens combination for imaging.
Use a 10X objective and 10X eyepiece for imaging.
Utilize a high-speed camera (≥1,000 fps) for visualization.
Perform necessary camera calibration prior to imaging.
Use image-based auto-trigger within the camera software to initiate image capture.
Mount the infinity chamber onto the microscope stage.
Secure the chamber by taping it into place on the stage.
Align the inkjet tip with the hole punctured in the natural rubber.
Bring the inkjet close to the chamber and adjust positioning by eye.
Make precise adjustments through the microscope lens for alignment.
Proceed cautiously during alignment to avoid damaging the inkjet tip.
Back the syringe assembly away from the chamber after alignment.
Ensure that motion of the inkjet is unidirectional.
Press gently on the plunger until a droplet forms at the inkjet nozzle.
Input jetting parameters: 20 kHz pulse frequency, 3 µsec rise time, 35 µsec pulse duration, 3 µsec fall time, and 65 V applied voltage with 100 jet pulses per trigger.
Add 25-30 μl lipid solution suspended in n-decane to the infinity chamber, covering both wells' surfaces.
Add 25 μl glucose slowly to one well's outer edge, forming a drop due to non-mixing with the lipid solution.
Add another 25 μl of glucose to the opposite well to form a lipid bilayer membrane within 5-10 minutes.
Insert inkjet through natural rubber and guide it towards the droplet interface bilayer slowly.
Apply the jetting with the settings described when the inkjet is within ~200 µm from the bilayer.
Clean the equipment by detaching the syringe assembly from the microscope stage and disposing of the 1 ml plastic syringe and filter.
Aspirate 70% ethanol through the tip 7-10 times.
Aspirate 2% Neutrad solution in warm water through the tip 7-10 times.
Aspirate 70% ethanol again through the tip 7-10 times.
Aspirate ddH2O through the tip 7-10 times if necessary to fit securely on the aspiration pipette.
Dry the chamber with tissue.
Place the infinity chamber in a 250 ml beaker with 2% v/v Neutrad in warm water and sonicate for 5-10 min.
Thoroughly dry the wells under compressed air after sonication.
Place the chambers in an oven at 60 °C for 15 min to ensure thorough drying.
